The Sacred Divide

Come in.

Four screens, about ninety seconds, and then you choose where to start.

Nothing here is tracked, stored, or sent anywhere. There is no account, no paywall, and no way for anyone to know you were here.

You can leave at any point and nothing follows you out.

One of two things to know

What this is.

  • A map of the machinery built around faith — the offices, the treasuries, the policies, and the people who benefit from your obedience.
  • Traced to documents: court judgments, government inquiries, regulatory orders, and the institutions’ own published rules.
  • Written so that you can keep the faith and refuse the leash.

Twenty-five traditions, each examined the same way, by the same standard.

Two of two

What this is not.

  • An argument that God does not exist.
  • A case that your faith is false, or foolish, or beneath you.
  • A campaign to get you to leave anything. No page here will ask you to.
  • A claim that the people who raised you meant you harm.

There is one place this does not soften: a practice that hurts people is not made holy by the language it wears.

If a sentence anywhere in this book fails that test, it is a defect in the book — not a discovery about you.

Now the only decision

Which tradition?

Pick the one you want to look at. Nothing is locked in — you can change it on the next screen, and every other tradition stays one tap away.

Before you start

One suggestion.

Nobody sees a pattern for the first time inside the thing that raised them. The defenses fire faster than the reading does.

If the one you chose is your own, consider spending six minutes somewhere unfamiliar first. Watch the machinery work where nothing is at stake for you, then come back holding a lens instead of a reflex.

Reading: —
Six minutes The six-minute version One ordinary day · one mechanism traced to whoever profits from it now · one thing the institution says beside the record · three questions. Complete in itself. Forty minutes The full page About forty minutes. Everything above, plus the history, the money, the roster of names, the eight stages with all thirty tactics, and your own objections answered.

Either one opens the whole site, with search and every other section one tap away. And at the bottom of the short version there is a door into the full page whenever you want it.
